title: Hangrend
summary: Every word is a back-vowel, front-vowel or mixed word. Endings change their vowel to match.

sections.text: Hungarian vowels come in two families. Which family a word's vowels belong to decides which version of an ending it takes. This is **hangrend** (vowel harmony), and it shows up in almost every grammar point from now on.

head: Type
Vowels
Examples
rows: only a á o ó u ú
only e é i í ö ő ü ű
back vowels + e, é, i, í

sections.text: Mixed words usually take **back** endings: *zsiráfban, kávéban, papírban*. Watch out when the **last vowel is a short e**: many of these take front endings instead: *hotelben, Bukarestben, fotelben*.
Why it matters: endings come in pairs
Many endings have a back version and a front version. You already met one: **-an / -en** (like English “-ly”): *lassú → lassan* (slowly). Soon you will meet **-ban / -ben** (“in”):
Try it: type any Hungarian word and see which family it belongs to.
